summary: 14-day telemetry demonstrates exceptional glycemic outcomes with 99.7% Time-in-Range (70–180 mg/dL), 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL), a mean glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, and low glycemic variability (CV 12.9%). The underlying AAPS profile and automation settings operate in close harmony, providing stable overnight basals and effective post-prandial coverage without driving hypoglycemia or requiring excessive loop compensation.
strengths: Near-optimal overall Time-in-Range of 99.7% with zero clinical hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) over 14 days.
Overnight glucose remains flat and stable between 102 and 108 mg/dL, confirming accurate baseline basal rates.
Effective meal strategy integration using prebolus timing, split bolus percentages, and e-carbs to keep post-prandial spikes well-controlled.
Low glycemic variability (CV = 12.9%), reflecting well-tuned ISF, CR, and DIA settings.
issues: Minor post-prandial peaks reaching up to 188 mg/dL following high-fat, high-carb weekend brunches.
education: When using AAPS with e-carbs, extended carbohydrate absorption is modeled in software rather than delivered as a traditional pump dual/square wave bolus. This allows SMB and UAM algorithms to dynamically adjust micro-dosing as actual digestion unfolds.
Setting prebolus timing according to meal glycemic index and fat content helps reduce 1- to 2-hour postprandial glucose excursions while preventing early post-meal drop.
safety_notes: Decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
Never alter insulin parameters without consulting your healthcare provider or clinical care team.
Maintain conservative safety limits (Max Basal and Max IOB) to protect against over-infusion during periods of sensor noise or delayed meal absorption.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain the current combination of 10–20 minute preboluses, 60–70% immediate bolus splits, active SMB/UAM automation, and 20g e-carbs over 120m for complex meals.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: This strategy effectively prevents sharp initial post-prandial spikes while permitting closed-loop automation to smoothly absorb remaining carb decay, achieving 99.7% Time-in-Range with zero hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Test extending the weekend brunch prebolus timing from 10 to 15 minutes to evaluate if the 120-minute post-prandial peak can be reduced below 180 mg/dL.

exceptions.rationale: Higher fat/protein content causes a delayed peak (~188 mg/dL at +120m); e-carb modeling enables SMB/UAM to cover the late rise safely.
